newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: BHP says Ok Tedi compensation deals signed.
newsitem.headline: BHP says Ok Tedi compensation deals signed.

text.p: The Broken Hill Pty Co Ltd (BHP) said on Friday two agreements had been signed which dealt with the compensation of communities and landowners affected by the Ok Tedi copper mine in Papua New Guinea (PNG).

The signing completed an out of court settlement by the mine's partners after about 600 landowners lodged a A$4 billion compensation claim against BHP in the Supreme Court of Victoria for environmental damages caused by Ok Tedi operations.
BHP owns 52.6 percent of the mine, the other partners being Canada's Inmet Mining Corp with 17.4 percent and the PNG government with 30 percent.
The two agreements signed were the Lower Ok Tedi agreement and the Lease Compensation agreement.

BHP said the Lower Ok Tedi agreement provided for payment of 40 million kina to communities living towards the lower reaches of the Ok Tedi river in PNG's Western Province that were most affected by mine's operations.
"This is in recognition of the greater impact which the mine has had on their lifestyles," the company said in a statement.

The settlement was additional to a general compensation package for people living throughout the Ok Tedi and Fly River systems of 110 million kina negotiated last year by the PNG Government and the Ok Tedi mine joint venturers.
The Lease Compensation agreement related to compensation of landholders of a Lease for Mining Purposes (LMP) which was granted to the joint venturers last month.
BHP said the LMP land would be used to deposit sediment from dredging of the lower section of Ok Tedi River as a part of the mine's tailings and waste rock management program.
BHP said dredging would take place over a period of two years during which time the mine partners would study the feasibility of a tailings pipeline from the mine's mill to the Lower Ok Tedi area.

The dredging and tailings pipeline options were two of four originally put forward by the company to minimise the environmental impact of mine tailings and overburden discharge. Ok Tedi produces about 600,000 tonnes of copper concentrate a year.

Concentrates are transported by pipeline from the mine to the port of Kiunga and then by barge down the Fly River for loading onto a silo vessel in the Gulf of Papua before being transferred to waiting bulk freighters.
